Files (all new):
- src/bin/g21_common/{mod,nlgen,extract,evalx,indep,pipe}.rs and src/bin/g21_{extract,verify,headline}.rs. g21_common reuses the g13 world via #[path].
- results/g21_*.{json,log} and results/g21_run_all.sh (rerun all, ~25 min, run alone).
- Quick rerun commands are in the board entry. selfcheck: `g21_verify.exe selfcheck --seeds 1-6`.

**Protocol:** the extractor was developed only against dev-bank text of tune seeds 1-8. Tuning on seeds 1-8, held 31-60, confirm 61-90, paired 95% t-CI, Holm over the 6 plain baselines. The W14 S1 reference is re-run in the same harness and reproduces W14 exactly (held A 0.8869, +0.2078).

**1. Extractor** (deterministic, std-only, with confidence and abstain; the NL generator, which I also wrote, has levels L0-L4, number words, distractors, typos, multi-step phrasing, and an UNSEEN phrasing bank the extractor was not built for)
- Spec accuracy checked by running the real tool on the extracted spec. Held, worlds A / B:
  - In-distribution phrasing: 96% / 91%. These are templates I wrote it for, so this is not a generalisation estimate.
  - Unseen phrasing: 52% / 39%.
  - By level, A: L0 .98, L1 .88, L2 .86, L3 .81, L4 .43.
  - Wrong spec delivered with confidence >= .6: 2.6% / 4.9% of compute tasks.
  - Confidence calibration: conf >= .9 is right 99.8% / 99.0%; .5-.7 only 69-75%.
- On prose tasks the extractor still emits a spec 17% / 27% of the time.

**2. Independent verifier**
- Second evaluator written from scratch: shunting-yard with fractions and f64 interval arithmetic, a unit table as decimal strings, csp certificate check, native re-implementation of the programs, optional metamorphic re-print.
- Mutation test: 21 seeded evaluator bugs (19 independent plus 2 common-mode) on 21,953 canonical specs per bug, held. Of 18,256 silent wrong outputs, the W14 shared verifier catches 19.2%, the independent one 90.0%.
- The independent verifier catches 100% of every non-common-mode bug; the shared one catches 0% of 12 of the 14 live independent bugs (E_idiv and E_round2 are partly caught).
- Common-mode bugs (planted in both paths) are caught 0%, so independence is only as good as the author's independence.
- On the stress corpus (random minimal-parenthesis expressions): shared 41.9%, independent 93.5%, metamorphic-only 55.1%.
- Selfcheck passes: the evaluator copy equals the real tools (4384/4384), the independent verifier has 0 false rejects, and a differential test of the real tools::Calc on 9000 random expressions found no bug.

**3. Headline: extractor + learned selector using confidence + independent verifier vs best fair baseline**

| set | best baseline | H - baseline (CI), all 30/0/0 | max Holm p | H cost/task (plain 10) | H as % of W14 lift |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| held A | keyword | +0.2055 [+0.1935,+0.2175] | 2e-24 | 13.5 | 99% |
| held B | guarded-safe | +0.1907 [+0.1748,+0.2066] | 3e-19 | 15.2 | 69% |
| confirm A | guarded-safe | +0.2178 [+0.2072,+0.2285] | 2e-27 | 13.4 | 102% |
| confirm B | guarded-safe | +0.1847 [+0.1702,+0.1993] | 3e-19 | 15.5 | 70% |

- What survives is mostly in-distribution phrasing. If all phrasing is unseen, the lift drops to +0.065 / +0.062. With only the phrasing the extractor was built for, it rises to +0.25 / +0.28.
- Not being given a clean spec costs -0.080 / -0.162 versus the same pipeline given the canonical spec. W14's lift mostly survives because extractor errors replace W14's simulated agent-formulation errors, not because extraction is easy.
- Verification value is about zero or slightly negative: indep - noverify is +0.002 / -0.006 (W14: +0.10), because the verifier re-checks the same wrong spec.
- The independent verifier on a correct evaluator changes correctness by +0.0002 (cost +0.03..0.08/task). End-to-end with one evaluator bug planted: +0.3..+1.4 pp over the shared verifier on extracted specs, +0.5..+2.7 pp on clean specs, 0 for common-mode bugs.
- Parser-class bugs have no effect on extracted specs, because the extractor fully parenthesises its output (accidental protection).
- The confidence rule (use the tool iff conf >= 0.4, tuned on seeds 1-8) BEATS the learned selector by 1.2-1.9 pp. The learned selector gains nothing from confidence features (-0.003, n.s.).
- A post-hoc kind-prior variant is flagged as such and is not in any headline.
- Cache: identical correctness (diff exactly 0), saves 0.53 / 1.12 cost units per task (A / B held), hit rate .21 / .28. Memo saves 1.4-1.6 more at +0.003 correctness (n.s.).
- vs vote3 (cost 30): +0.136 / +0.111 held.

**4. Controls (all-prose worlds, TOST ±0.01)**
- The learned arm: -0.002..-0.003, TOST true in all 4 cells, but the diff is non-zero in 3 of 4; cost +0.5..0.65.
- The confidence rule FAILS: -0.8 to -3.3 pp, TOST false. Needs a prose guard.

**Honest limits:** everything depends on my own NL generator and extractor; the unseen bank is only unseen to my extractor. The extractor still delivers confident wrong specs on 2.6% / 4.9% of compute tasks, which no verifier here can see. A second extractor or the agent's own formulation as a spec-level cross-check is the untested next step (in the proposals file).
